title: How courts actually evaluate expert and forensic witness testimony
p1:
A confident expert can still lose credibility in court.

Many people assume judges and juries simply trust the person with the most impressive title. The reality is far more interesting.
p2:
Courts do not evaluate expert testimony by confidence alone. They look at how the expert reached their opinion, whether the methods are reliable, and whether the evidence actually supports the conclusion.

A surprising fact: an expert can be highly qualified and still have their testimony given little weight if their reasoning is weak or their approach cannot be tested.
p3:
The strongest forensic testimony is not the one with the biggest words. It is the one where the evidence, method, and explanation connect clearly.

A useful lesson for any professional: expertise is not just about what you know. It is also about how you prove your thinking can be trusted.
conclusion: What do you think matters more in evaluating an expert: their credentials or the quality of their reasoning?
